newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dell sees smooth change to new Europe head.
newsitem.headline: Dell sees smooth change to new Europe head.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp expected a smooth transition in leadership after naming a successor to the chief who turned around its European units.

Dell last week named Jan Gesmar-Larsen, former head of Apple Computer Inc. in Europe, to take over for Martyn Radcliffe, president of Dell Europe, who was leaving to become a corporate turnaround specialist.
Gesmar-Larsen was expected to take over his duties in August under an extended transition plan.
"It's not abrupt, so it shouldn't be much of a disturbance to our business," Hans-Juergen Mammitzsch, managing director of Dell's German unit, told Reuters on Thursday.
But he conceded Radcliffe's departure was a loss for the company. "He saved the company in Europe," Mammitzsch said.
After Radcliffe joined Dell in 1994, the company refocused its strategy on direct marketing computers to business customers and sales in the region rose from $782 million to more than $2 billion.
